title: Slavery's origins and musicians' ordinary backgrounds
summary: Hinton talks about African traders in slavery, and both note musicians come from ordinary backgrounds.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: Well, you know, you go back to this business about slavery. Who the hell sold them the slaves in the first place? The black chieftans would sell slaves, the Arab traders. The only slavery country today is in Africa. Then later the Americans and English would go raid and cut out the middleman, but in the beginning they were selling their own people.
I tell you, it sure gives us a great perspective, as musicians, because most of us have come from ordinary backgrounds, none of us have --
Oh, yeah, very few musicians come from rich backgrounds.
And it's given us a chance. And to be able to travel when you're sort of -- you know, when you can look at it in this perspective.
